summary: Deep skeptical per-feature audit of SteamProject to find vaporware, bugs, security holes, and backend gaps

result.feature: Authentication & Identity (Steam OpenID login, register, account management)
result.summary: The core auth actually works: ASP.NET Core Identity is wired correctly (AddDefaultIdentity + cookie + AddSteam OpenID), password login with a seeded user succeeds end-to-end (verified live: TestUser@mail.com / TestPassword123! logs in and redirects home), registration creates both an IdentityUser and a paired app User row, and Steam OpenID linking is genuinely implemented in Manage/ExternalLogins (challenge -> Steam -> LinkLoginCallback parses the SteamId out of the OpenID provider key, checks a blacklist, and persists it). This is NOT vaporware. However there are real gaps: the entire Views/Authentication/* (Index.cshtml, Signin.cshtml) folder is dead code with no controller (no AuthenticationController exists, /Authentication and /signin both 404); the custom Login.cshtml strips out the external-login (Steam) button so Steam sign-in is only discoverable after you already have a password account; SteamController and UserController are completely unprotected ([ApiController]/Controller with NO [Authorize] and NO ownership checks) enabling IDOR and unauthenticated state mutation; and several auth-related catch blocks swallow/rethrow opaquely. The confirmation-email flow relies on the framework default-UI pages (ConfirmEmail/RegisterConfirmation/ForgotPassword exist via the Microsoft.AspNetCore.Identity.UI 8.0 package, confirmed ForgotPassword returns 200), so registration confirmation is functional but untested against a real SendGrid key (key is optional and silently no-ops).

security.desc: SteamController (Controllers/SteamController.cs) is [ApiController] with NO [Authorize] on the controller or any action. State-mutating endpoints POST /api/Steam/follow, /unfollow, /hide, /unhide, PATCH /setNickname, /revertNickname, POST /UpdateTheme, and especially POST /DeleteComp (deletes ANY competition by id, line 249-264) are callable by unauthenticated users. DeleteComp takes a raw compId and deletes it with no ownership/role check = unauthenticated arbitrary competition deletion.

UserController (Controllers/UserController.cs) is a fully unprotected scaffold: NO [Authorize] anywhere. Index lists ALL users, Details/Edit/Delete operate on any user id with no ownership check (IDOR). Edit/Create bind SteamId/SteamName directly, so an unauthenticated request can rewrite or delete any user's profile and reassign Steam IDs.

Steam follow/unfollow/hide/unhide endpoints accept arbitrary userId/id and operate without verifying the target belongs to the caller (e.g., SteamController.Hide line 80-88 trusts the userId form value). IDOR on game state for any user.
SteamController.SendInvite (line 193) lets anyone send arbitrary emails through the configured SendGrid account to any address (open email relay / spam vector), unauthenticated.

Cookie auth does not set Cookie.SecurePolicy/HttpOnly explicitly (Program.cs:92-97 only sets LoginPath/LogoutPath); relies on defaults. CorrelationCookie.SecurePolicy=Always for Steam is set, but app cookie hardening (SameSite, expiration, sliding) is not configured.

result.backendLeverage: The Identity/EF backend is genuinely leveraged for the happy paths: login, register (dual-write to Identity + SteamInfo), Steam OpenID link/unlink, blacklist check, and admin ban all hit real repositories and DbContexts. Where it falls short: (1) the bespoke Views/Authentication/* UI is wired to nothing and duplicates functionality the Identity area already provides; (2) the canonical Login page does not surface the Steam external-login that the backend fully supports, so a major backend capability (Steam-first auth) is unreachable from the primary UI; (3) authorization is the biggest gap - the backend has working role infrastructure (AddRoles, admin seeding, [Authorize(Roles=\"admin\")] on AdminController) but the API surface (SteamController/UserController) bypasses it entirely; (4) two separate DbContexts for one logical user are coordinated without transactions.
uxIssues: Login page offers no Steam sign-in button at all; users must register a password account first, then dig into Profile > Steam Account to link Steam - backwards for a Steam social app.
Dead /Authentication and /signin pages will 404 if any old link or bookmark points to them.
In development with no SendGrid key, registration appears to succeed but the user is silently stuck (no confirmation email, cannot log in, no error shown) - extremely confusing.
Steam unlink performs destructive cascading deletes (all games, all friends, all achievements) with no confirmation dialog shown in the markup.
Logout in the _LoginPartial layout may not actually log the user out (GET vs POST handler mismatch).
Login page error messaging is generic ('Invalid login attempt.') and does not distinguish unconfirmed-email from wrong-password.

result.feature: Game Library (follow/hide games, achievements, owned games, recommendations, genre/category filtering)
result.summary: The core Library does work end-to-end: LibraryController.Index pulls owned games from the Steam Web API on refresh, persists Game + UserGameInfo rows via EF, and renders them; client-side filtering by genre/category/search is real and functional; the achievements modal fetches live Steam data. However the mutation endpoints (hide/unhide/follow/unfollow) live in SteamController, which has NO [Authorize] and NO global auth policy, so they are reachable unauthenticated and hide/unhide trust an attacker-supplied userId (IDOR). I verified POST /api/Steam/hide?id=1&userId=1 returns 500 (not 401), GET /api/Steam/achievements returns data with no auth, and follow 500s unauthenticated due to GetUser(null). The follow/unfollow JS also fires its success callback synchronously instead of as a callback, so the UI updates regardless of whether the server call succeeded. The GameAchievementRepository/UserAchievementRepository listed in the manifest are not used by Library at all (only CompeteController); Library achievements are purely live Steam API with no persistence.

security.desc: SteamController (Controllers/SteamController.cs:14) has [ApiController] but NO [Authorize] at class or action level, and Program.cs:109 uses AddControllersWithViews with no global AuthorizeFilter/FallbackPolicy. All Library mutation/read endpoints (hide, unhide, follow, unfollow, achievements, schema, games, friends) are reachable unauthenticated. Verified live.

IDOR on hide/unhide: SteamController.Hide/Unhide (lines 80-98) act on a userId supplied in the query string with no check that it matches the authenticated user. Combined with no auth, anyone can mutate any user's hidden-games state.

Information disclosure: GET /api/Steam/achievements, /schema, /games, /sharedGames, /friends require no auth and accept arbitrary steamid/userId, leaking any Steam user's owned games, achievements, and friends through this app. Verified /api/Steam/achievements returns a response unauthenticated.

No antiforgery protection on the POST mutation endpoints (hide/unhide/follow/unfollow). They are [ApiController] cookie-authenticated state-changing POSTs invoked via jQuery AJAX with no token; CSRF-exploitable once auth is added unless tokens or a non-cookie scheme is enforced.
ShowMoreInfo (LibraryController.cs:318) lacks [Authorize] (only Index has it) and returns UserGameInfo without OwnerId filtering, leaking another user's playtime for a shared game.
Steam Web API key (_token) is interpolated into outbound URLs; ensure it is sourced from config/secrets and never logged. Endpoints echo Steam errors; confirm no key leakage in 500 responses.

result.backendLeverage: The UI leverages the backend reasonably for the read path: the library grid, filters, recommendations, and the achievements modal are all backed by real controller actions, EF repositories, and live Steam API calls rather than fake data. The real gaps are: (1) all write/mutation actions live in an unauthenticated, IDOR-prone SteamController instead of the [Authorize]d LibraryController, so the UI is effectively trusting client-supplied userId; (2) two repositories in the feature manifest (GameAchievementRepository, UserAchievementRepository) and their DB tables are not leveraged by Library at all — achievements are recomputed live from Steam on every modal open with no caching/persistence, an unnecessary external dependency on every interaction; (3) the Sort action/view is orphaned, replaced by client-side filtering; (4) follow/hide success handlers are wired to fire optimistically, so the UI does not actually reflect backend success/failure.
uxIssues: Follow/hide icons update optimistically (success callback invoked synchronously), so on a server error the UI lies about state until a manual page reload.
Hidden Games modal requires a manual page refresh to reflect newly hidden games (the empty-state message even instructs 'try refreshing the page').
errorOnAjax only console.logs; users get no toast/feedback when follow/hide fails (refresh has a toast via SteamNexusToast, but follow/hide do not).
Refresh re-imports the entire library and re-hits the Steam store API per game for genre enrichment; on large libraries this is slow with only a generic spinner overlay.

Apostrophe handling in game names is done by string-splicing a backslash into onclick attributes (Index.cshtml:119-122) instead of proper encoding/data attributes; fragile for names with multiple quotes or other special chars.
achievement ratio/progress bar uses player achievement count as denominator and a magic *200 px width, so the bar can mis-scale across games.

There is hardcoded test data faking an achievement for a specific SteamId in the leaderboard path.

result.feature: Friends & Blacklist (add/remove friends, block, friend activity)
result.summary: The "Friends" feature is really a read-only mirror of the user's Steam friends list plus a game-comparison page; it is NOT a friend-management system. There is no add-friend, remove-friend, or accept-request flow in the app at all, and there is no user-facing "block" feature - the BlackList model is exclusively an admin ban tool, mislabeled by the manifest. What does work: pulling the Steam friends list on first visit, caching it in the DB, showing online status/current game via polling, comparing shared games and achievements, and setting/reverting a per-friend nickname. The entire mutation and data surface lives on SteamController, which has ZERO [Authorize] attributes - every endpoint (friends list, nickname edit, email invite) is reachable anonymously, with no ownership checks (IDOR) and no antiforgery. The "Invite friend to Team" button is wired to nothing, and several actions throw 500s on missing data instead of handling it.

result.feature: Inbox / Messaging (compose, send, read messages, email/SMS notifications)
result.summary: A real-time-ish chat widget and a static inbox table both exist and are wired end-to-end to SQL Server: contacts load from the friends list, conversations load via messagesBetween, and messages persist via sendMessageTo. I verified live against localhost:5105 that messages send and persist. However the entire messaging API (MessagesController) has ZERO authentication and takes fromId/messengerId as untrusted query parameters, so any unauthenticated caller can read anyone's conversations and send messages spoofing any sender (verified: I posted a message as user 2 to user 1 with no credentials and read it back). The "email notifications" claim is partly real (SendGrid via EmailSender) but is NOT wired to the inbox feature at all; the SendToInbox method that builds Sender/Subject/Content rich inbox messages is dead code (never called), and "SMS notifications" do not exist anywhere in the codebase. There is no unread/read state, no mark-as-read, and sending to a nonexistent recipient throws an unhandled 500 that leaks the full DB schema and stack trace.

result.summary: This feature is genuinely wired end-to-end and is NOT vaporware: the dashboard and ShowMoreNews views call real API endpoints (NewsController) that fetch live Steam news via ISteamNews/GetNewsForApp and summarize it through a real OpenAI gpt-4o-mini ChatCompletion call. A real OpenAI key is configured in user secrets ("OpenAiKey": "sk-proj-..."), the Betalgo.OpenAI v8.7.2 package is referenced, and the controller is [Authorize]-gated (verified live: /api/News/GetRecentGameNews returns 302 to login when unauthenticated). The gaps are robustness and quality, not fakeness: the controller calls the [Obsolete] synchronous GetGameNews wrapper which does sync-over-async (.GetAwaiter().GetResult()) risking thread-pool starvation/deadlock under load; an unguarded NullReferenceException path exists when the Steam API fails (_poco is null but the try block only wraps the OpenAI call); SingleOrDefault() is used where the list may have multiple items; and there is no server-side caching so every uncached dashboard tile fires a paid OpenAI call. The summarization is sound and the UI presents it with localStorage caching, typewriter animation, and skeleton loaders.

security.desc: Stored-XSS-adjacent: summarizeSpecificNews.js:75 and 147 write cached summaries to the DOM via innerHTML (newsElement.innerHTML = storedNews). The content originates from OpenAI output cached in localStorage; while same-origin-only and AI-sourced, using innerHTML for model output that could contain markup/script is risky. The fresh-fetch path safely uses typeWriter textContent, but the cache path bypasses it.

ShowMoreNews.cshtml:43 renders <a href="@item.url"> directly from Steam-supplied news item URL with no scheme validation; a javascript: or malicious URL from the feed would render as a clickable link. Razor encodes the attribute value but does not block dangerous schemes.

No rate limiting / cost control on the OpenAI-backed endpoints. An authenticated user can loop GetSpecificGameNews/GetRecentGameNews with arbitrary appIds and incur unbounded paid OpenAI calls (server-side has no cache; only client localStorage caches).

result.backendLeverage: The UI leverages the backend well for the happy path: every news tile and the Summarize buttons hit real controller actions backed by live Steam ISteamNews calls and real OpenAI ChatCompletion summarization, with sensible client-side localStorage caching and loading states. Gaps: (1) The controller calls the deprecated synchronous SteamService.GetGameNews wrapper rather than awaiting GetGameNewsAsync, so the genuinely-async backend is consumed in a blocking way. (2) There is no server-side caching of summaries, so the only thing preventing repeated paid OpenAI calls is per-browser localStorage — a different browser/device re-summarizes and re-pays. (3) Error responses are inconsistent: GetRecentGameNews returns 200 Ok with a friendly string but can also throw 500 on null _poco; the JS only branches on data.summarizedNews truthiness and otherwise logs to console, so backend failure messages ('User not found', BadRequest bodies) never surface to the user. (4) The newsIndex contract between ShowMoreNews.cshtml (10-item render) and GetSpecificGameNews (fetch newsIndex+1 with post-filtering) is not robustly aligned.

No visible cost/latency feedback: a cold dashboard with many tiles fires many sequential OpenAI calls, each taking seconds; tiles fill in staggered with no aggregate progress indicator.

The Summarize toggle relies on comparing normalized innerText to data-original-content (summarizeSpecificNews.js:62); if whitespace normalization differs the toggle can mis-detect state and fail to switch back.
ShowMoreNews.cshtml uses a <head> block inside the body (line 7) and pulls bootstrap from a CDN inside the partial — non-standard and can double-load assets if the layout already includes Bootstrap.
Summary cache TTL is 1h client-side only; a returning user on another device always re-pays/re-waits with no shared cache.

result.summary: The SteamService HTTP client is the most genuinely-built part of this feature: it is a real, async, IHttpClientFactory-based client with consistent try/catch, structured logging, and graceful null returns across ~12 Steam Web API endpoints (player summaries, level, friends, owned games, app details, news, achievements, schema, GAP).
